newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit stays rangebound in Asian trading.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit stays rangebound in Asian trading.

text.p: The ringgit stayed within a tight range in Asian trading after falling earlier against the dollar on covering of short dollar positions, dealers said.
They said lack of fresh leads and an unexpectedly huge Malaysian trade deficit in April announced on Friday limited demand for the ringgit.
Malaysia announced a trade deficit of 2.1 billion ringgit in April after a 1.75 billion ringgit surplus in March.
"I think offshore funds were discouraged from buying ringgit by the April trade deficit," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.

Earlier, the market was also unloading ringgit positions taken ahead of the weekend in case the Bank Negara meeting with chief executives of some banks on Friday led to some surprises. The meeting ended without any announcement of a shift in the central bank's policy.
Offshore players had sold dollar/ringgit aggressively on Thursday on fears that Bank negara may impose capital controls like those of Thailand.
Dealers said players were also waiting for April money supply figures which could give some indications on whether the central bank would ease its monetary policy stance.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5155/65 a dollar against 2.5131/41 at close in Kuala Lumpur on Friday.
Dealers said that though the dollar appeared to be supported at 2.5130/40, corporate sales out of Kuala Lumpur could continue to cap its rise around 2.5180.
